Introduction

Artificial intelligence has evolved from symbolic reasoning to data-driven systems, yet its foundational assumptions remain under negotiation (as we formalize below: ((((([{{{{{}}}}}]))))). In this paper, we investigate how AI systems can be understood as layered adaptive processes that integrate statistical learning, symbolic reasoning, and human-in-the-loop evaluation. By framing intelligence as a hierarchical and interpretable structure, we develop a framework for analyzing model behavior, accountability, and alignment. This approach not only clarifies the interaction between data, architecture, and decision-making, but also provides a basis for more transparent and reliable artificial intelligence.
